  "concordance_definition": "A quantitative formula that integrates multiple features (EDA 1, EDA 2, DEA 1, DEA 2, Clustering, ML) to quantify how strongly a given dog cancer recapitulates a human cancer, with a score ranging from 0 to 1, where 1 indicates perfect similarity.",
  "limitations_stated": [
    "Dog tumors are not universally strong models of human tumors.",
    "Many lack a rigorous scientific evaluation of the molecular parallels between dog and human tumors.",
    "The extent to which a particular dog cancer faithfully models its human counterpart remains unclear.",
    "No pancancer transcriptomic analysis of human and dog tumors exists to date.",
    "The formula focuses on broader cancer-level similarities, which can obscure subtype-specific heterogeneity.",
    "Inconsistencies in annotation granularity between dog and human datasets.",
    "The relative scarcity of well-established cross-species studies at fine-grained resolution across both species limits the availability of positive controls."
  ],
  "funding_conflict": null,
  "key_numbers": [
    "5,875 samples (913 dogs and 4,962 human samples, including 806 pediatric samples) spanning 11 tumor types.",
    "Mean difference of 0.1007 (95% CI: 0.10067–0.10081) between cancer type effect and species effect.",
    "Adult cancers generally showed high concordance between species.",
    "Pediatric cancers showed more score variability.",
    "Model robustness scores ranged from 31% to 85%.",
    "Negative controls (ACC, LAML) scored 31% and 40%.",
    "Formula feature weights: EDA 1 = 0.002, EDA 2 = 0.085, DEA 1 = 0.029, DEA 2 = 0.159, Clustering = 0.665, ML = 0.060.",
    "Elastic net model had the highest performance for adult samples (AUC 0.92).",
    "Random forest model was the best model for pediatric samples (AUC 0.99).",
    "Adult BLCA had the lowest percentage of cancer-specific DEGs (0%).",
    "DLBC had the highest percentage of cancer-specific DEGs (24%) in adult cancers.",
    "ACC had the lowest percentage of cancer-specific DEGs (0%) in pediatric cancers.",
    "OS had the highest percentage of cancer-specific DEGs (7%) in pediatric cancers.",
    "GBM/LGG in pediatric samples showed relatively strong enrichment of COSMIC cancer genes (P-value = 2.70 × 10−2).",
    "OS in pediatric samples showed relatively strong enrichment of COSMIC cancer genes (P-value = 1.60 × 10−2).",
    "Dog tumors mirror the organ-system level structure previously seen in adult cancers.",
    "Mean difference of 0.046 (95% CI: 0.0460–0.0469) for adult GBM/LGG subtype heterogeneity.",
    "Mean difference of 0.033 (95% CI: 0.0321–0.0341) for adult SARC subtype heterogeneity.",
    "Mean difference of 0.060 (95% CI: 0.0594–0.0603) for pediatric GBM/LGG subtype heterogeneity.",
    "Mean difference of 0.024 (95% CI: 0.0226–0.0251) for pediatric SARC subtype heterogeneity."
  ]
